items.title: Bill Kirchner interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 4, 2021
items.q: He had just gotten off Woody Herman’s band.

ctx.x: Were you ever tempted at that time to call up Mom and Dad and say, “Listen, I’m not going to major anymore in what I’m doing, I have to be a musician.”

No. I didn’t have the guts. Plus I was, you know, this was my excuse for being in New York. So I mean I was studying with Konitz for a couple of years and then I started studying for a couple of years with Harold Danko, who by the way is also from Youngstown, Ohio, although I used to play outdoor concerts with his older brothers who were both saxophone players. We would play concert band gigs in Youngstown. And I didn’t meet Harold until 1973 when we were both in New York. He had just gotten off Woody Herman’s…

It seems that your career has been a series of opportunities that came up that you managed to step into and succeed. If you went to a gathering, a cocktail party or something, and it was just a brief conversation with somebody you really didn’t know and they said, “What do you do?” Do you have like a brief answer?
